45-MINUTE MOCK INTERVIEW

Debug a real codebase,
on the clock.

Investigate a real issue, fix it, extend it, and explain your design — with an interviewer asking follow-ups and a deliberately limited local AI beside you.

Set up your interview

The codebase is downloaded and its environment prepared before the clock starts. Real GitHub tasks come from SWE-bench Multilingual with their original issue and regression tests; they can need several GB of disk and some minutes to prepare. A pasted repository has no known failing test, so you choose what to investigate and which test command to run.

Everything runs on your machine. The copilot is small enough to be wrong — checking it is part of the exercise.

Set up your local gym

The app runs on your computer. Two local services power the practice environment.

1. Start Docker

Docker Desktop on macOS and Windows, or the Docker daemon on Linux; Windows additionally needs WSL 2. Runtime images download automatically the first time you run tests. Code executes without network access and cannot write to your host files.

Benchmark images are published for x86_64 only, so on Apple Silicon they run under emulation and are slower. Enable Rosetta in Docker Desktop → Settings → General for the best speed.

2. Start Ollama

Get Ollama from ollama.com. Pick which local model plays each role — the copilot is meant to be small enough to be wrong, the interviewer needs room to hold a conversation.

16 runtime presets are available for imported code. The random task library covers 9 languages and supplies task-specific images. Generic images supply compilers, but project dependencies may need a custom prepared image.
